header.userPrompt:
Make every code-producing built-in flow end with a best-effort pull request, and make the end-of-run branch handling follow the run target instead of a per-flow flag.

## Goal

Almost every built-in flow follows the same shape: understand (plan), code, review loop. Add a fourth, uniform final step: open a PR whenever the repository is detected to be on GitHub and GitHub is reachable. This is best effort: if it is not a GitHub repository, or GitHub cannot be reached / `gh` is not authenticated for that host, the flow says so in one line ("not a GitHub repository, no PR opened" / "cannot reach GitHub (<reason>), no PR opened") and finishes successfully without a PR. It must work for github.com and for self-hosted GitHub (GitHub Enterprise Server on any hostname).

## What to build

1. **GitHub detection built-in.** Add to the built-in tools (`GitHubTool`, `package orca.tools`) a read-only probe answering whether a PR can be opened from this checkout, as an enum, not booleans: e.g. `NoRemote`, `NotGitHub(host)`, `Unreachable(host, reason)` (gh not installed / not authenticated for that host / network), `Available(host, owner, repo)`. Derive the host from the `origin` remote URL (both ssh `git@host:path` and URL forms — `OsGitTool.remoteHost` already parses this; move or share it rather than duplicating). Treat github.com AND any host that `gh` recognises as a GitHub instance as GitHub — e.g. `gh auth status --hostname <host>` and/or `gh repo view --json owner,name` run against that host — do not hardcode github.com as the only GitHub host. Wire an `OsGitHubTool` implementation and a fake for tests.

2. **Self-hosted support in the existing PR code.** `OsGitHubTool.PrUrlPattern` and `PrHandle.url` hardcode `https://github.com/...`. Make them host-aware (e.g. `PrHandle` carries the host, or the URL is parsed generically by `<scheme>://<host>/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<n>`), so `createPr` / `findOpenPr` work on GHES. `PrHandle` travels through `JsonData` — no defaults on its fields (0.x rule in AGENTS.md).

3. **Best-effort PR helper in `orca.pr`.** Add a flow-level helper next to `openPrFromBranch` (e.g. `openPrIfGitHub(summarisingAgent = ..., ...)` returning `Option[PrHandle]`) that runs the probe first, and on anything but `Available` emits a single `OrcaEvent.Step` naming the reason and the next action, then returns `None`; on `Available` it pushes, summarises and creates the PR through the existing stages. The probe is a read and stays outside stages; push/summarise/create keep the existing three-stage split (resume safety — see `openPrFromBranch`'s scaladoc). Keep `openPrFromBranch` for flows that REQUIRE GitHub (the issue-driven ones), or implement it on top of the new one — one decision, one home.

4. **Branch handoff follows the run target.** Today `flow(..., returnToStartBranch: Boolean = false)` is a static per-flow choice, and `FlowLifecycle.finishBranch` acts on it. Replace that with a rule derived from `OrcaArgs.target` (`RunTarget`) and whether the run actually opened a PR — the invoking checkout should be left the way it was found:
   - `RunTarget.NewBranch`: when the flow opened a PR, check the start branch back out (the feature branch stays, pushed). When no PR was opened (not GitHub / unreachable), stay on the feature branch as today, so the user ends on the work; the closing summary already names the branch.
   - `RunTarget.Worktree`: never switch branches — the worktree stays on its `orca-worktree-<hash>` branch and the invoking checkout is untouched (already the case; keep it that way and make sure the PR step runs from inside the worktree).
   - `RunTarget.CurrentBranch` (`--skip-branch`): still push and open the PR best-effort from that branch, but never change what is checked out.
   Remove the `returnToStartBranch` parameter from `flow`/`runFlow`/`FlowLifecycle.run` and every call site (built-in flows, tests, README). The lifecycle needs to learn that a PR was opened: the PR helper records it on the flow context/control (a small, explicit door — no global mutable state; follow the capability conventions in AGENTS.md), and `teardownSuccess` reads it. The throwaway-branch deletion rule in `finishBranch` stays as is.

5. **Built-in flows.** Append the best-effort PR step to `flows/implement.sc`, `flows/implement-interactive.sc`, `flows/simple.sc`, and switch `flows/implement-enhanced.sc`, `flows/issue-pr.sc`, `flows/issue-pr-bugfix.sc` off `returnToStartBranch = true`. The issue flows may keep requiring GitHub (they read the issue from it). `flows/review.sc` produces no code and gets no PR step. Update each flow's header comment and the one-line description on its first line. Note `orca create`/`orca fork` run `simple.sc` in a sandbox that is not a GitHub repo — the best-effort step must skip cleanly there (check `shell/.../create` for how the sandbox is set up and add/adjust a test if there is one).

6. **Docs and tests.** Update README ("The flow lifecycle" success-teardown paragraph, the built-in tools section, the flows/CLI sections mentioning PRs, any mention of `returnToStartBranch`) and AGENTS.md where the lifecycle description changes. Unit tests use the existing fakes (`StubCliRunner`, `TestFlowControl`, `orca.testkit.GitRepo`) — cover: the probe's enum outcomes from stubbed `gh`/`git` output (github.com, a GHES host, a non-GitHub host, no remote, gh unauthenticated); host-aware PR URL parsing; the helper's skip path emitting the reason; and `finishBranch` for each `RunTarget` × PR-opened/not. Run `sbt scalafmtAll`, `sbt compile` and `sbt test` (the full suite) before finishing; fix warnings under `-Wunused:all`. `ORCA_INTEGRATION=1 sbt publishLocal "shell/testOnly *BuiltInFlowsCompileTest"` compiles the built-in flows against the local build — run it, since the flow scripts change.

## Constraints

- Follow AGENTS.md: enums over booleans for modes, no defaults on persisted/domain fields, no back-compat shims, comments only for what the code cannot say, no history in comments, every user-facing refusal names the next action.
- Agents are trusted but fallible; do not justify any design by adversarial agent behaviour.
- Subprocess calls go through `CliRunner`/`QuietProc` (stderr captured), never raw `os.proc(...).call`.
- Do not commit-message-attribute anything to an AI; do not touch `.orca/settings.properties`.
